report.previous_run_delta: New: OpenAI committed $1B to subsidized Daybreak access for frontline defenders, but the individual award and solo-builder fit are unquantified. Recovered: AWS Activate Founders offers a direct $1,000 bootstrap tier with conditional top-up to $5,000, and its sequencing conflict with Kiro is now explicit. New: AREX-Skill/DisCo makes verified operational knowledge portable across agents. Strengthening: Astra moved from announced-soon to a live API release. New but currently mismatched: NVIDIA PAIR. Closed: WebMCP submissions passed their September 3 1 p.m. PT deadline. Deepgram, Zoho, AssemblyAI, Cloudflare, and AMD were unchanged and not recycled.

signals.classification: CONFIRMED FACT; INDIVIDUAL AWARD AND FIT UNDETERMINED
signals.changed: OpenAI announced a $1B global commitment on September 3 for subsidized Daybreak access, training, technical support, and partnerships, targeted for consumption over six months.
signals.free_value: Subsidized frontier cyber-model access and support; prior affected water-system support reached up to $1M in no-cost API credits, but no standard per-applicant amount is published.
signals.fit: Prioritizes U.S. essential-service operators, state/local government, community banks, nonprofits, open-source maintainers, and supporting organizations with constrained security resources.
signals.catch: The aggregate $1B headline is not an applicant entitlement. A new small open-source repository alone is not evidence of frontline-defender fit, and Daybreak requires verified, authorized defensive use.

signals.changed: Recovered and resolved the bootstrap tier and sequencing conflict: self-funded founders start with $1,000 in AWS credits and select participants may reach $5,000; active Activate users are excluded from Kiro startup credits, while Kiro recipients may apply to Activate afterward.
signals.free_value: $1,000 initial AWS Activate Founders credits; up to $5,000 conditional total.
signals.fit: Direct application is available to self-funded, pre-Series-B companies founded within ten years. No investor Org ID is required.
signals.catch: Requires an AWS Paid Tier account and professional email; overages are billable. Kiro's separate offer requires VC backing, matching domain email/AWS account, IAM Identity Center, activates immediately, and auto-switches to paid billing.

signals.changed: A September 2 paper formalized DisCo and the AREX-Skill library: 5,000+ verified operational skills distilled from 1,000 repositories, compatible with Codex and other coding agents.
signals.free_value: Apache-2.0 repository-level library and MIT DisCo CLI; selective skill import and refresh workflows are available without software fees.
signals.fit: Directly tests ICE's thesis that timestamped provenance and reusable operating knowledge can compound agent capability.
signals.catch: Model-provider inference can cost money; Node 22.19+ is required; each skill has its own authoritative license; imported skills and scripts create supply-chain and instruction-trust risk.

signals.classification: CONFIRMED FRESH API LAUNCH; NO FREE API SUBSIDY
signals.changed: GPT-6 Astra moved from announced-soon to released in the API on September 3, with long-running-work controls including asynchronous tool calling and mid-turn steering.
signals.free_value: No free API allocation was verified. Access through an existing paid ChatGPT plan was not directly observed.
signals.fit: Potential labor replacement for difficult end-to-end coding, research, computer-use, and document workflows.
signals.catch: API pricing is $10 input/$50 output per million short-context tokens on the model page; long context is more expensive. Production monitoring can pause or stop work, and high-authority tasks still require scoped permissions and review.

signals.classification: CONFIRMED FRESH OPEN-SOURCE RELEASE; CURRENT HARDWARE MISMATCH
signals.changed: NVIDIA released PAIR on September 3, an Apache-2.0 local router that discovers LAN nodes and exposes Ollama/OpenAI-compatible endpoints for independent inference requests.
signals.free_value: Router software for Windows, Linux, and macOS; prompts can remain local when every client, model source, engine, and node is local.
signals.fit: Could coordinate future RTX/Apple-silicon devices for multi-agent workloads.
signals.catch: It does not pool VRAM, shard models, or create compute. The user's present single non-RTX machine does not gain useful capacity from it, and LAN endpoints/security need review.

omissions_errors: Daybreak does not publish individual subsidy amounts or guarantee acceptance; the $1B figure is a global commitment, not a per-applicant entitlement.
The user's actual AWS Activate/Kiro application and credit state was not observable.
AREX benchmark improvements are author-reported and were not independently reproduced in this run.
GPT-6 Astra API availability was verified, but availability in the user's ChatGPT account was not observed.
PAIR is free software but does not create compute and is poorly matched to the user's present non-RTX single-device hardware.
Google Agents for Impact was inspected but omitted from recommendations because the near-term events require travel and no program-specific infrastructure grant was verified.
